title: Canonical affine embedding of an intersection of quasi-compact opens
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] every quasi-compact open of which is quasi-affine (a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme). Let $E\subset |Y|$ be an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens. Give $E$ its subspace topology and the inverse-image sheaf [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] $\mathcal O_Y|_E$. Put $C=\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)$. Then $(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)$ is a locally ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and there is a unique morphism of locally ringed spaces
$$j_E:(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose map on global sections $C\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}C,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)=C$ is the identity; for every open $L\subset Y$ contained in $E$, the restriction $j_E|_L$ is the morphism corresponding to the restriction map $C\to\Gamma(L,\mathcal O_Y)$. This $j_E$ identifies its source with $(F,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}C}|_F)$ for a subset $F\subset\operatorname{Spec}C$ that is an intersection of quasi-compact opens. For every open subscheme $W\subset Y$ with $W\subset E$, $j_E|_W$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. The construction is natural for isomorphisms of schemes carrying the indicated subsets to one another.

proof.text: For quasi-compact opens P,Q, their union is quasi-affine. Its canonical affine open embedding [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] reduces compactness of P intersection Q to [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] makes Y quasi-separated. Index ALL quasi-compact open neighborhoods of E, ordered by reverse inclusion. This is a Type u family even when the original family has a larger index universe. It is nonempty, directed by intersection, and its intersection is E because it includes the original opens. Apply [lem-a1-sections-intersection-structure-colimit], reindex its distinct-open diagram, and use each chart top-section isomorphism to identify its cocone with global-section pullback along E to the chart.

By [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk], the restricted sheaf has local stalks $\mathcal O_{Y,e}$. The affine adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] gives the unique normalized $j_E$. Its naturality gives $p_i j_E=j_i|_E$ and the claimed restriction formula on every ambient open $L\subseteq E$. Here $j_i$ is the canonical map of $U_i$ and $p_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\to C)$.

Apply [lem-a1-quasi-affine-chart-limit-topology] to this directed family and colimit. The displayed compatibility identifies its unique continuous map with $j_E$, hence $j_E:E\to F=\bigcap_i p_i^{-1}(j_i(U_i))$ is a homeomorphism and the intersected opens are quasi-compact.

For $e\in E$ and $\mathfrak p_i=j_i(e)$, the open immersion $j_i$ [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] and the spectrum stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](1) identify $(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ with $\mathcal O_{Y,e}=\mathcal O_{E,e}$. These are the germ maps by step 2 and the inverse-image stalk identification. Apply [lem-a1-affinization-localization-stalk-criterion] to $Z=E$: it identifies $j_E$ with an isomorphism onto the inverse-image ringed subspace on $F$.

For an ambient open W contained in E, lift its inclusion to the locally ringed subspace using the inverse-image adjunction. The chart-limit lemma [lem-a1-quasi-affine-chart-limit-topology] says that j_E(W) is open. The lift is an embedding, and its stalk maps are isomorphisms because both ambient inclusions have that property. Together with the stalk isomorphisms of j_E, [def-weil-open-immersion] gives the required open immersion. Naturality of the affine adjunction gives its stated restriction formula.

If $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde Y$ carries $E$ onto $\widetilde E$, its restriction is an isomorphism of the restricted locally ringed spaces and induces a ring isomorphism $\widetilde C\to C$ on sections. The two composites from $E$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde C$, namely $j_{\widetilde E}\circ h|_E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\widetilde C\to C)\circ j_E$, correspond to this same ring homomorphism. They are equal by [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction]. This proves naturality, independently of all choices of the family or of $U_0$.
